question: After factor-wise oracle headroom was established, can runtime observables safely admit depth correction, or can the independently positive R21 angular-boundary factor produce a strict body-swept task gain?

runtime_correction_gain_observability.protocol: Fourteen consumed TUM parents, leave-one-parent-out threshold selection, source depth opened only after RGB/K inference, parent-wise MAE and >0.10 m error no-regret, at least half of parents nonzero.

naive_boundary_to_task_intervention.protocol: On one already-consumed ICL synthetic-exact parent, hold source-exact depth, support and obstacle fixed; replace only boundary probability with frozen R20 or R21 output before the unchanged adapter/reducer.
naive_boundary_to_task_intervention.interpretation: R21 affects downstream task states and is closer to source reference than R20, but treating boundary absence as negative obstacle evidence can emit unsupported CLEAR and is inadmissible.

fail_closed_boundary_binding.binding: Boundary absence never lowers positive obstacle evidence; component-edge disagreement can only increase boundary localization sigma and therefore preserve or degrade task state to UNKNOWN.
fail_closed_boundary_binding.interpretation: The one-sided binding restores fail-closed semantics, but R20 and R21 become task-identical. R21 therefore remains valid boundary-localization evidence but has no strict body-swept task gain on this consumed parent.

decision.next_successor_scope: Prediction-first consumed Development substitution audit: compare source-reference task states against learned-support-only, learned-obstacle-only and learned-support-plus-obstacle arms from the frozen R14/R21 factor family. No training, task-threshold tuning or boundary-map retry.

claim_boundary: Consumed Development mechanism evidence only. It stops the current correction router and boundary-to-task mapping attempts. It does not establish complete task superiority, independent cross-sensor generalization, deployment, product readiness, default-App eligibility, navigation utility or assistive safety.
